flashcard_questions.q: Why does every computer need secondary storage as well as memory?
flashcard_questions.a: It is non-volatile, so it keeps files and programs permanently without power.

flashcard_questions.q: How does magnetic storage record data on a hard disk drive?
flashcard_questions.a: As magnetised patterns on the surface of fast-spinning metal platters.

flashcard_questions.q: Which part of a hard disk drive detects and changes the magnetism?
Why is a hard disk drive easier to damage than a solid-state drive?
flashcard_questions.a: It has moving parts: spinning platters and a head that travels across them.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main strength of a magnetic hard disk drive?
flashcard_questions.a: Very high capacity at a very low cost per gigabyte.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is magnetic tape too slow for everyday use?
flashcard_questions.a: It is sequential, so the drive must wind through the tape in order.

flashcard_questions.q: How does an optical drive read data from a disc?
flashcard_questions.a: A laser shines on the track and the reflection shows a 1 or 0.

flashcard_questions.q: What are the tiny bumps and flat areas on an optical disc called?
Roughly how much data does a CD hold?
What is the approximate capacity of a single-layer DVD?
What is the approximate capacity of a single-layer Blu-ray disc?
Why is solid-state storage faster and more durable than a magnetic drive?
flashcard_questions.a: It has no moving parts at all.

flashcard_questions.q: What limits how long each cell in solid-state storage lasts?
flashcard_questions.a: Each cell can only be rewritten a limited number of times.

flashcard_questions.q: Which secondary storage suits backing up a large amount of data cheaply?
flashcard_questions.a: Magnetic tape or a high-capacity hard disk drive.
